wizard.title: New campaign
wizard.createdRegistering: Campaign created. Mosaic registration is running in the background...

advancedOptions.title: Advanced options
advancedOptions.description: Most campaigns should keep the default access settings. Expand to choose who can label, complete tasks, or edit other people's annotations.

campaign.nameHint: Pick a name that a colleague would recognise months from now - e.g. “Malawi maize 2024” rather than “test 3”.

access.title: Labelling access
access.description: Every campaign supports both task-by-task labelling and free exploration - annotators can switch between them anytime from the annotation view. The rules below decide who may label what, and whose labels count toward completing a task. You can change all of this later in campaign settings.
access.rulesHint: Each rule is a list of groups. Hover a group to see who it means. Leaving a rule empty turns that activity off for everyone.
access.membersHint: Members come from the project - manage them under the project’s Members tab.

review.intro: Review everything before creating the campaign.

settings.labelsDescription: Define the different classes that annotators can assign to shapes / that they can choose from when labeling.
settings.labelsExample: <label>Example:</label> For a crop survey you might want to identify all fields with Maize, Cassava or Fallow, aswell as Farms. These would be your class names. You only need to select a geometry type for each class if you are planning on allowing users to draw the shapes of these. In our case, you would select polygon as the geometry types for the 3 field types and might want to select point for a farm.
settings.formDescription: Add extra questions for annotations. These allow you to capture additional details beyond the main class label.
settings.formExample: If you just drew a Maize field you might want to distinguish the crop stage of the fields. So you could specify a “Crop stage?” custom field with “Crop stage?” and “Seedling / Mature / Harvested” as options.
settings.embeddingDescription: Experimental. If set, satellite embeddings are fetched for the chosen year to enable KNN-based label validation during annotation: a new label is checked against the embeddings of every existing one. Leave it at None unless you plan to use this.

importFeatures.title: Import Existing Features
importFeatures.description: Upload a GeoJSON file of existing features. Each feature must carry a stacnotator_label_id property whose value is one of this campaign's label ids (listed below). The import is rejected if any feature is missing a label or uses a label id that does not belong to this campaign.
importFeatures.noLabels: This campaign has no labels defined.
importFeatures.confirm: I confirm the label ids in my file match the label ids of this campaign.

assignSelected.everyUser: Every selected user on every task
assignSelected.distribute: Distribute tasks evenly among selected users

taskScope.needsOneSet: A campaign needs at least one task set
taskScope.deleteDescription_one: This permanently deletes the set and its {{count}} task(s) with all associated annotations. This action cannot be undone.
taskScope.deleteDescription_other: This permanently deletes the set and its {{count}} task(s) with all associated annotations. This action cannot be undone.

vectorLayers.title: Vector layers (PMTiles)
vectorLayers.description: Toggle them on or off while annotating, hover to highlight, and label features by clicking with the Label vector tool.
vectorLayers.loadError: Could not load the vector layers.
vectorLayers.name: Name

hints.archive: Must be a PMTiles vector archive (`.pmtiles`) -read directly by the browser, no tiler required.
hints.https: Reachable over HTTPS -a public URL, or one that includes a SAS token.
hints.sourceLayer: Set a source layer to render just one layer inside the archive; leave blank for all.

duplicate.title: Duplicate "{{name}}"
duplicate.intro: Creates a new campaign with the same setup: imagery sources and visualizations, views and layouts, labels and forms, labelling policy, time series, basemaps and overlays. Adjust the copy afterwards in its settings.
duplicate.adminOnlyHint: Only projects you administer can receive a campaign.
duplicate.crossProjectNotice: Annotations, task assignments and personal layouts are not copied into another project - the people they name need not be members there. Only the setup, and the task locations if you keep them, come along.

tasks.title: Also duplicate tasks?
tasks.crossProject: Copies all task locations and task sets. They arrive unassigned, with no progress.
tasks.sameProject: Copies all task locations and task sets. Task progress starts fresh unless annotations are copied too.

assignments.title: Keep task assignments?
assignments.body: Copies the explicit assignments to annotators. Without them every task in the copy is open for anyone to pick up. Tasks a labelling agent holds always arrive free: an agent is registered for one campaign and cannot work the copy.

annotations.title: Also duplicate annotations?
annotations.body: Copies every existing label with its author and timestamps into the new campaign.

layouts.title: Keep personal layouts?
layouts.body: Copies the canvas window arrangements individual users saved for themselves.

duplicate.withoutTasksNotice: Without tasks, only annotations that are not linked to a task (Explore labels) are copied.

assignAll.title: Assign All Tasks
assignAll.evenlyHelp: All unassigned/ not yet completed tasks are split as evenly as possible across the selected users. Each user receives either ⌊N/users⌋ or ⌈N/users⌉ tasks, assigned in random order.
assignAll.fixedHelp: Each user receives the exact number of tasks you specify. Tasks are drawn randomly from the pool; once a task is taken it won't be assigned to anyone else.
assignAll.previewEven_one: Preview: Will assign {{count}} tasks evenly distributed across {{users}} user(s)
assignAll.previewEven_other: Preview: Will assign {{count}} tasks evenly distributed across {{users}} user(s)

policy.noMembers: No members in this project yet.
policy.noOne: No one - this axis is disabled.

admins.label: Admins
admins.help: Admins of the project this campaign belongs to. They always keep full access.

authoritative.label: Authoritative reviewers
authoritative.help: Project members marked as authoritative reviewers, under the project’s Members tab. Their labels are the ones treated as the reference when annotators disagree.

assignees.label: Assignees
assignees.help: Whoever a task is assigned to - each person, on their own tasks only.

members.label: Members
members.help: Everybody in the project, whatever their role.

anyone.label: Anyone (public visitors)
anyone.help: Visitors with no account, reaching the campaign through its public link. Only available while the project is public.

explore.title: Explorative labelling
explore.description: Who may create free-form, standalone annotations that are not tied to a task.
explore.example: With Members, any project member can draw their own polygon anywhere on the map and label it. Everyone else can still browse the imagery, but their drawing tools stay off.

unassigned_tasks.title: Unassigned tasks
unassigned_tasks.description: Who may label a task nobody is assigned to, and whose label counts toward completing it.
unassigned_tasks.example: A campaign of 500 points that annotators work through first come, first served. With Members, any project member can pick one up and their label completes it on its own.

assigned_tasks.title: Assigned tasks - additional labels
assigned_tasks.description: Who may add extra labels to a task that is already assigned to someone else. Extra labels are shown alongside the assignee’s but do not necessarily count toward completion.
assigned_tasks.example: Point #42 is assigned to Alice. With Authoritative reviewers, a reviewer can add a second label beside hers for comparison. Picking up a task from the unassigned pool assigns it as well, so this rule applies to it from then on.

complete_assigned.title: Assigned tasks - completion
complete_assigned.description: Whose labels on an assigned task count toward completing it, including satisfying review requirements.
complete_assigned.example: Point #42 is assigned to Alice and needs one review. Her label plus a reviewer’s marks it done. A label from anyone outside this list is still stored and shown, but the task stays open.

modify_others.title: Editing and deleting other people’s annotations
modify_others.description: Who may change or remove an annotation somebody else made. Everyone can always change their own.
modify_others.example: With Admins, an annotator who spots a mistake in a colleague’s polygon can open it and read it, but not move or delete it. With Members, the campaign becomes a shared canvas that any member can correct.

reviewerAssign.title: Set Up Task Reviews
reviewerAssign.percentageHelp_one: A random subset of tasks will be selected for review. For each selected task, {{count}} user(s) from your pool will be assigned to review it.
reviewerAssign.percentageHelp_other: A random subset of tasks will be selected for review. For each selected task, {{count}} user(s) from your pool will be assigned to review it.
reviewerAssign.fixedHelp_one: An exact number of randomly selected tasks will each be reviewed by {{count}} user(s) from your pool.
reviewerAssign.fixedHelp_other: An exact number of randomly selected tasks will each be reviewed by {{count}} user(s) from your pool.
reviewerAssign.poolHelp_one: The system randomly picks {{count}} of these users per task. Users are never assigned to review a task they originally annotated. Select at least {{count}}.
reviewerAssign.poolHelp_other: The system randomly picks {{count}} of these users per task. Users are never assigned to review a task they originally annotated. Select at least {{count}}.
reviewerAssign.preview_one: Preview: Randomly assign {{reviewers}} reviewer(s) from your {{pool}}-person pool to each of the {{count}} selected tasks. Users won't review tasks they annotated.
reviewerAssign.preview_other: Preview: Randomly assign {{reviewers}} reviewer(s) from your {{pool}}-person pool to each of the {{count}} selected tasks. Users won't review tasks they annotated.

sampling.title: Generate Tasks via Sampling
sampling.description: Generate annotation tasks by sampling points within a region. You can either upload a boundary file or use the campaign's bounding box.

random.label: Random Sampling
random.description: Randomly sample points within the region

grid.label: Grid Sampling
grid.description: Sample a regular grid of points, a fixed distance apart

grid.title: How the grid is drawn
grid.spacing: Spacing is ground distance, so points stay the same distance apart everywhere in the region, however far north or south it reaches.
grid.offset: The grid is placed at a random offset rather than pinned to a corner, so it cannot line up with roads, field edges or anything else laid out regularly.
grid.order: Tasks are created in random order, so stopping part way through still leaves the whole region covered.

errors.noRegion: Please select a region file or use campaign bounding box
errors.minSamples: Number of samples must be at least 1
errors.spacing: Grid spacing must be greater than 0 km
errors.seed: Seed must be a whole number of 0 or more

sampling.useBboxHint: Sample within the campaign's defined area
sampling.spacingHint: Distance between neighbouring points. The number of tasks follows from the size of the region.
sampling.seedHintGrid: Fixes the offset the grid is placed at, so the same seed redraws the same grid
sampling.seedHintRandom: Set a seed for reproducible sampling results

tasksTab.addIntro: Tasks define the points or polygons annotators will label. Upload existing locations or generate them with random/grid sampling into {{name}}.
tasksTab.uploadFileHint: Upload tasks from CSV or GeoJSON
tasksTab.generateHint: Create tasks using random or grid sampling
tasksTab.uploadHelp: Upload a CSV (id,lon,lat) for point locations, or a GeoJSON file with Point / Polygon features. Polygon geometries are preserved and shown as sample extents during annotation. For Points you may want to specify the sample extent (bbox size around the point) under the General Settings tab. The id must be unique within your whole campaign and must be numeric.
tasksTab.heading: Annotation tasks
tasksTab.assignmentsButtonTitle: Export or import who these tasks are assigned to
tasksTab.selectSetFirst: Select the task set to upload or generate tasks into.

empty.locked: No sampling units drawn yet. They appear here once the design above is finished.
empty.readOnly: No annotation tasks in this set yet.
empty.all: No annotation tasks yet. Select a set to upload or generate tasks.
empty.set: No tasks in this set yet. Add tasks to upload a file or generate them.

tasksTab.assignmentsDescription: Who each task is assigned to and who reviews it, as a CSV to edit and upload again. This never creates or removes tasks.

timeseriesStep.title: Optional: Timeseries
timeseriesStep.description: Graphs that plot a single pixel's value over time: at the annotated point the chosen spectral index is computed across the date range and drawn as a chart beside the imagery.
timeseriesStep.panelsDescription: Panels organize timeseries on the annotation page. All series in a panel appear together. For example, put series for 2022 in one panel and series for 2023 in another, so each panel shows a manageable date range instead of one extremely long timeseries.
timeseriesStep.optionalHint: Timeseries are optional. Leave the initial blank series untouched to skip them.
timeseriesStep.duplicatePanel: A panel with this name already exists.
timeseriesStep.name: Timeseries name

estimate.modalBody: An area estimate turns a classified map and a sample of checked points into a published area with a confidence interval. Its points live in their own task set, managed by the design.
estimate.name: Name
estimate.nameHint: What this estimate covers, and for when.

errors.taskOutput: Failed to update the task output

toasts.researchOn: Annotations from this campaign may now be published as research data

renameLabels.title: Rename existing labels?
renameLabels.description_one: Renaming labels affects how existing annotations display - the underlying label IDs stay the same, so no data is lost, but every annotation tagged with this label will now show the new name everywhere (review, exports, statistics).
renameLabels.description_other: Renaming labels affects how existing annotations display - the underlying label IDs stay the same, so no data is lost, but every annotation tagged with these labels will now show the new name everywhere (review, exports, statistics).

deleteFields.description_one: Saving deletes {{names}} and permanently deletes every answer annotators have recorded for it across all annotations in this campaign. This cannot be undone.
deleteFields.description_other: Saving deletes {{names}} and permanently deletes every answer annotators have recorded for them across all annotations in this campaign. This cannot be undone.

editFields.title: Edit existing form fields?
editFields.description_one: Editing fields affects how existing annotations display - the underlying field IDs stay the same, so stored answers are kept, but annotators will see the updated question everywhere (annotation view, review, exports).
editFields.description_other: Editing fields affects how existing annotations display - the underlying field IDs stay the same, so stored answers are kept, but annotators will see the updated questions everywhere (annotation view, review, exports).

recompute.title: Recompute Embeddings?
recompute.description: Changing the embedding year from {{from}} to {{to}} will delete all existing embeddings and re-fetch them from the satellite imagery for {{to}}. This may take a while for large campaigns.

name.title: Campaign name
name.description: The display name shown across the app.

guide.title: Campaign guide
guide.description: Markdown document shown to annotators via the book icon in the annotation toolbar.
guide.placeholder:
# Campaign Guide

Write instructions for annotators here using Markdown...

research.title: Research data sharing
research.description: Allow the annotations created in this campaign to be published as open research data, without any annotator's name. Off by default. Turning it off stops future releases - anything already published cannot be recalled. See the Terms of Service.
research.label: Publishable as research data

taskOutput.title: Task output
taskOutput.description: What finishes a task: picking a label for the task's own point or polygon, or drawing shapes around it. Fixed once the first task has been annotated.
taskOutput.label: Tasks are finished by

extent.title: Sample extent
extent.description: Defines the exact size of a sample point. If lat/lon is the exact coordinate, the sample extent defines the dimensions around this centroid that constitute the actual sample. This helps to have a shared understanding of which area / pixels belong to a sample point. Leave empty if tasks were uploaded as polygons or if no extent should be visualized.
extent.label: Extent (meters)

labels.title: Annotation labels
labels.description: The class names annotators choose from when labeling. You can add new labels and rename existing ones; renaming requires confirmation since it affects how prior annotations display. Deleting labels is not supported (it would orphan existing annotations).
labels.invalid: Label names must be non-empty and unique.

formFields.title: Custom form fields
formFields.description: Additional questions annotators answer per annotation. You can add new fields and edit existing ones; editing requires confirmation since it affects how prior answers display. Deleting a field also deletes every answer recorded for it, so it asks first. A field's type or options can only change while it has no answers yet.

policy.description: Control who may label what, and whose labels count toward completing a task. Members and visibility are managed at the project level - <link>open project members</link>.

embedding.description: The year from which satellite embeddings are sourced for KNN-based label validation. Changing this will recompute all embeddings for the campaign.
embedding.notSet: No embedding year set - KNN-embeddings (AEF) based validation is currently unavailable for annotators.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.description: Once you delete a campaign, there is no going back.

bbox.title: Region of Interest
bbox.description: The region of interest defines your study region and limits the geographic area in which imagery will be prepared.
bbox.sourceNote: Boxes are derived from Natural Earth and OpenStreetMap boundaries and cover core national territory only. They are a starting point to drag, not an authoritative boundary.
bbox.dragHint: Drag the corner handles to resize, or drag the box to move it

customMaps.title: Raster layers (COG)
customMaps.description: Predictions or classifications drawn over the imagery, toggled from the viewer’s panel.
customMaps.loadError: Could not load the raster layers.

hints.cog: Must be a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) - internally tiled with overviews so the tiler can read only the pixels it needs.
hints.singleBand: Single-band raster (e.g. a class map or probability layer).
hints.reachable: Reachable by the tiler. For private Azure storage, provide a SAS token separately below so it is saved encrypted, not in the URL.
hints.projection: Any projection with a WGS84 datum (UTM zones and EPSG:4326/3857 are all handled).
hints.notValidated: Not validated automatically - an invalid or non-COG file will not render.

customMaps.replaceToken: Paste a new token to replace it
customMaps.experimentHint: Linked from an icon next to the map, e.g. the MLflow run that produced it.
customMaps.internalStorageHint: Check this if the file lives in our own Azure storage, so the tiler reads it with its managed identity. Leave unchecked for public or AWS-hosted files.
